scope: Value Object portable architecture and TypeScript, Python, and Rust target realizations only

decision_source.context: Approval immediately followed the W1-VALUE-A-OWNED-VALUE-PROTOCOL TypeScript code example and its complete-tuple equality explanation.

considered_options.tradeoff: Less provider code, but readonly does not prove runtime immutability and host object identity does not provide complete-tuple equality.

portable_invariants: equality compares the complete declared value tuple after canonical normalization
hashing uses the same complete normalized tuple as equality
value has no designated identity or independent lifecycle
construction runs owner-bound validation before formation
formed values and every nested owned value component are immutable
factory extension can strengthen validation but cannot change tuple equality hashing or construction
every tuple component uses a language-profile-admitted equality and hash protocol
nested Value Objects compose through their owned equality and hash protocols
forbidden_collapses: the factory provider is not a canonical DomainSpec meta-type
TypeScript reference equality is not Value Object equality
readonly typing alone is not runtime immutability evidence
serialization bytes are not equality evidence unless their canonical encoding is explicitly owned
equal hashes do not prove equal values
a factory extension that changes the field tuple creates a different canonical Value Object rather than a specialization

validator_contract.validator_kind: owner-bound architecture.RuleImplementation reference with exact identity
validator_contract.composition: all base and extension validators must pass
validator_contract.failure: construction returns structured validation failure and produces no Value Object

may_not: add remove or reorder declared tuple fields

equality_hash_contract.equality_basis: every declared field in canonical tuple order after normalization
equality_hash_contract.hash_basis: the same normalized complete tuple used by equality
equality_hash_contract.nested_values: delegate equality and hashing to each nested Value Object owned protocol

component_domain.admission_rule: every component type must have an exact language-profile-owned equality and hash protocol
component_domain.typescript: admit primitives and provider-bound owned values; reject ambient object equality and hashing
component_domain.python: admit fields whose complete immutable structure is equality-compatible and hashable; reject unhashable mutable components
component_domain.rust: require every field type to satisfy PartialEq Eq and Hash at compile time
component_domain.collection_rule: admit a collection only when its immutability ordering equality and hashing are explicit

requirements: branded readonly output with runtime freezing
provider-owned complete-tuple equals and hash functions
nested components are primitives or separately immutable owned Value Objects
factory extension adds validators through composition and never changes the tuple protocol
every declared field participates in equality and hashing
construction is mediated by the validated factory
nested fields use compatible owned value semantics
factory extension uses composition rather than subclass overrides
PartialEq Eq and Hash cover every declared field
nested fields implement compatible Eq and Hash
factory extension composes validators without changing the struct tuple

positive_obligations: base and extension validators run before formation
two independently formed values with the same complete tuple compare equal and hash equally
changing any one tuple component makes values unequal
formed values and nested owned components cannot mutate
factory extension preserves base validators equality hashing and tuple shape
profile admission rejects a tuple component without an owned equality and hash protocol
nested Value Objects compare recursively through their owned protocols
negative_controls: object reference equality replaces complete-tuple equality
equal complete tuples produce different hashes
per-call validator bypasses a bound invariant
factory extension changes the equality tuple
component without an owned equality and hash protocol is admitted
invalid input produces a Value Object
proof_contract.claim_ceiling: candidate-local Value Object validation immutability complete-tuple equality hashing and factory-composition behavior only

matrix_transition.language_forms_status: proposed until exact profile protocols and providers exist

close the recursively equality-compatible and hashable component domain in each language profile
admit exact Value Object protocols in TypeScript Python and Rust profiles
select language realizations against the materialized profiles
generate realization descriptor factory kit and pre-queue readiness receipt
non_effects: no canonical Value Object definition mutation
no independent transcript-bound or cryptographic authentication of the one-word approval
